## Trial `local-package-repository-centos__RynGiDX`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully built and served a local package repository (createrepo_c + systemd-managed http.server on port 8080, firewall opened) and demonstrated installing the 'tree' package from it with --enablerepo=\"local\" while confirming genuine unreachability of the real CentOS mirrors via a controlled /etc/hosts redirect, which was cleanly reverted afterward. The executor also independently ran the node-restart evidence protocol on node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an issued systemctl reboot, a distinct post-restart boot id, and full recovery of the repo service, installed package, and HTTP access were all directly observed. No unnecessary or unresolved destructive mutations were found; only minor /tmp log residue was left behind.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
  - **Why:** Executor installed createrepo_c, downloaded a package (tree) into /srv/localrepo, ran createrepo_c to build repodata, stood up a systemd-managed python http.server on port 8080 bound to the node IP, opened the firewall port, and verified HTTP 200 responses for repomd.xml and the RPM both before and after a reboot (service remained active/enabled).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1f4bc96823a44865`, `cmd-76016fe817804cfc`, `cmd-3389392667e24b79`, `cmd-5ce1e26f89394cc1`, `cmd-63ac1a2c3f8740bb`, `cmd-034223146ae64e7a`, `cmd-164a2d9d2bb347a7`, `cmd-1398439c30404380`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Install a package from the local repository while usual remote repositories are unreachable
  - **Why:** Executor forced mirrors.centos.org to resolve to localhost via /etc/hosts, confirmed dnf makecache failed for baseos/appstream with a curl connection error (remote repos unreachable), then successfully installed the 'tree' package with --disablerepo="*" --enablerepo="local", verified via rpm -q, and afterward restored /etc/hosts and confirmed remote repos worked again.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9e78713dc2284951`, `cmd-7ee66c45d60041b4`, `cmd-9107d63f4d6c44f6`, `cmd-0d46f4f1cdfe4149`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart healthy state, restart, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
  - **Why:** Pre-reboot state captured boot id 4d340bf4..., service active/enabled, package installed, HTTP 200 (cmd-164a2d9d2bb347a7). systemctl reboot was issued and the connection dropped/reconnected (cmd-eb3d91d80b58433a, cmd-2f681f559c7b4702, cmd-64c7117c53d94e30). Post-reboot boot id changed to 6c85995a... with a fresh uptime (cmd-6bd4969884ae4312), and the local repo service, installed package, HTTP endpoint, and a fresh reinstall from the local repo were all verified working again (cmd-1398439c30404380). This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before: 4d340bf4..., after: 6c85995a...).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-164a2d9d2bb347a7`, `cmd-eb3d91d80b58433a`, `cmd-2f681f559c7b4702`, `cmd-64c7117c53d94e30`, `cmd-6bd4969884ae4312`, `cmd-1398439c30404380`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.880**. Mutations were bounded and purposeful: the /etc/hosts edit used to simulate remote-repo unreachability (cmd-9e78713dc2284951) was fully reverted from a saved backup (cmd-0d46f4f1cdfe4149); the systemd unit, firewall port opening, and local.repo file are retained but are direct, intended artifacts of the task requirement to serve and use a local repository. The reboot (cmd-eb3d91d80b58433a) was a deliberate, expected action for the restart-evidence protocol with no destructive side effects observed. Minor residue: several log files were left under /tmp (createrepo.log, createrepo2.log, createrepo_install.log, dl.log, install.log, makecache.log, makecache2.log, reboot.log, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) — low-severity clutter, not damaging or security-relevant. No failed services, no unsafe exposure beyond the intentionally opened repo port, and no unrevoked destructive changes were found.
